ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an ideal op-amp circuit. The inverting terminal of the op-amp is connected to the upper feedback voltage-divider node: one end of this node is connected to ground through R1=10 kΩ, and the other end is connected to the output node on the right side through R2=100 kΩ. The non-inverting terminal of the op-amp is connected to the input test node on the lower left side, and the arrow of current Ix points from the left-side port to this node; this non-inverting input node is also connected to the output node on the right side through R3=1 MΩ. The black dot on the right side is the op-amp output node, and Vx is marked beside it in the figure. Reasoning: To eliminate sign ambiguity, although Vx is marked beside the output node on the right side in the figure, when the problem writes the input resistance as RIN=Vx/Ix, according to the definition of input resistance, interpret Vx as the input terminal test voltage; below, denote the input terminal voltage as Vx, and denote the output node voltage on the right side separately as Vo. The ideal op-amp input current is zero, and the negative feedback network R1 and R2 makes the circuit become a non-inverting amplifier with respect to the non-inverting terminal, so Vo=(1+R2/R1)Vx=(1+100kΩ/10kΩ)Vx=11Vx. Since the non-inverting input terminal does not absorb current, the injected Ix can only flow through R3 to the output node, so Ix=(Vx−Vo)/R3=(Vx−11Vx)/1MΩ=−10Vx/1MΩ=−Vx/100kΩ. Therefore RIN=Vx/Ix=−100 kΩ.

raw_record.question_text: What is the input resistance \(R_{IN} = \frac{V_x}{I_x}\) of the circuit shown in the figure?

method.method_draft: First identify from the image the standard non-inverting amplifier feedback network: R1=10 kΩ to ground and R2=100 kΩ from output to the inverting input, so for an ideal op amp Vo=(1+R2/R1)Vin=11Vin, where Vin is the voltage at the input test node connected to the + input. Since the op-amp input draws no current, the injected current Ix at that node must flow through R3=1 MΩ toward the output: Ix=(Vin−Vo)/R3=(Vin−11Vin)/1 MΩ=−10Vin/1 MΩ. Therefore Rin=Vin/Ix=−(1 MΩ)/10=−100 kΩ.
